report:
This claim is well supported by primary regulatory evidence.

**FDA approval and labeling:** The official FDA-approved label states directly: "Kyleena is a progestin-containing intrauterine system (IUS) indicated for prevention of pregnancy for up to 5 years" (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/208224s000lbl.pdf). This is corroborated by DailyMed's structured product labeling, which repeats the same indication verbatim and notes the drug was first approved in the U.S. (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080).

**Manufacturer documentation:** Bayer's own product monograph confirms that "following insertion into the uterine cavity, KYLEENA...is effective for up to 5 years" and states it "must be removed by the end of the fifth year," with replacement possible at that time if continued contraception is desired (https://www.bayer.com/sites/default/files/2020-11/kyleena-pm-en.pdf).

**Clinical trial data supporting the approval:** According to drug history reporting, FDA approval was based on a Phase III clinical trial of 1,452 women aged 18–35, showing a Pearl Index of 0.29 after five years and greater than 99% annual effectiveness in preventing pregnancy (https://www.drugs.com/history/kyleena.html). This aligns with DailyMed's note that a 3-year phase 3 study was extended with an optional continuation to 5 years to support the 5-year indication.

**Conclusion:** The claim is accurate. Kyleena is FDA-approved for pregnancy prevention for up to 5 years, based on the official FDA label, DailyMed prescribing information, Bayer's product monograph, and supporting Phase III trial data. It differs from other levonorgestrel IUDs (e.g., Mirena, approved for up to 8 years; Skyla, 3 years), so duration should not be generalized across the product class.
